sanskrit: ye ca vedavido viprā ye cādhyātmavido janāḥ te vadanti mahātmānaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dharmaṃ sanātanam
english: Those brahmins who know the Vedas and those people who know the inner self declare that the great-souled Krishna is the eternal Dharma.

sanskrit: pavitrāṇāṃ hi govindaḥ pavitraṃ param ucyate puṇyānām api puṇyo 'sau maṅgalānāṃ ca maṅgalam
english: Govinda is declared to be the highest of all purifying things; he is the most meritorious of all meritorious things and the most auspicious of all auspicious things.

sanskrit: trailokyaṃ puṇḍarīkākṣo devadevaḥ sanātanaḥ āste harir acintyātmā tatraiva madhusūdanaḥ
english: The lotus-eyed one, the eternal god of gods, Hari of incomprehensible nature — that very Madhusudana dwells there in the three worlds.

sanskrit: dhaumya uvāca avantiṣu pratīcyāṃ vai kīrtayiṣyāmi te diśi yāni tatra pavitrāṇi puṇyāny āyatanāni ca
english: Dhaumya said: In the western direction, in the land of Avanti, I shall describe to you the sacred and holy shrines that exist there.

sanskrit: priyaṅgvāmravanopetā vānīravanamālinī pratyaksrotā nadī puṇyā narmadā tatra bhārata
english: O Bharata, there is the sacred river Narmada, adorned with groves of priyangu and mango trees, garlanded with forests of reeds, flowing with its current toward the east.

sanskrit: niketaḥ khyāyate puṇyo yatra viśravaso muneḥ jajñe dhanapatir yatra kubero naravāhanaḥ
english: There is renowned a sacred abode where Kubera, the lord of wealth who rides men, was born as the son of the sage Vishravas.

sanskrit: vaiḍūryaśikharo nāma puṇyo girivaraḥ śubhaḥ divyapuṣpaphalās tatra pādapā haritacchadāḥ
english: There is a holy and auspicious mountain called Vaidurya-shikhara, where trees with green foliage bear divine flowers and fruits.

sanskrit: tasya śailasya śikhare saras tatra ca dhīmataḥ praphullanalinaṃ rājan devagandharvasevitam
english: On the peak of that mountain, O king, there is a lake of the wise one, covered with blooming lotuses, frequented by gods and gandharvas.

sanskrit: bahvāścaryaṃ mahārāja dṛśyate tatra parvate puṇye svargopame divye nityaṃ devarṣisevite
english: O great king, many wonders are seen on that holy mountain, which resembles heaven, is divine, and is ever frequented by divine sages.

sanskrit: hradinī puṇyatīrthā ca rājarṣes tatra vai sarit viśvāmitranadī pārā puṇyā parapuraṃjaya
english: O conqueror of enemy cities, there too is the Vishvamitra river with its sacred fords, the holy river of the royal sage, and the far bank is sacred.

sanskrit: yasyās tīre satāṃ madhye yayātir nahuṣātmajaḥ papāta sa punar lokāṃl lebhe dharmān sanātanān
english: On the bank of that river, in the midst of the righteous, Yayati, son of Nahusha, fell; but he regained the worlds and the eternal dharmas.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyahradas tāta mainākaś caiva parvataḥ bahumūlaphalo vīra asito nāma parvataḥ
english: There, dear one, is a sacred lake, and the Mainaka mountain; and, O hero, there is the mountain called Asita, rich in roots and fruits.

sanskrit: āśramaḥ kakṣasenasya puṇyas tatra yudhiṣṭhira cyavanasyāśramaś caiva khyātaḥ sarvatra pāṇḍava tatrālpenaiva sidhyanti mānavās tapasā vibho
english: There, O Yudhishthira, is the sacred hermitage of Kakshena, and also the renowned hermitage of Chyavana, known everywhere, O Pandava; and there, O lord, people attain perfection with but little austerity.

sanskrit: jambūmārgo mahārāja ṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām āśramaḥ śāmyatāṃ śreṣṭha mṛgadvijagaṇāyutaḥ
english: O great king, the Jambu road is the hermitage of sages of purified soul, the best of peaceful places, thronged with flocks of deer and birds.

sanskrit: tataḥ puṇyatamā rājan satataṃ tāpasāyutā ketumālā ca medhyā ca gaṅgāraṇyaṃ ca bhūmipa khyātaṃ ca saindhavāraṇyaṃ puṇyaṃ dvijaniṣevitam
english: Beyond that, O king, are the most sacred regions always filled with ascetics — Ketumala, Medhya, the Ganga forest, O lord of the earth, and the renowned Saindhava forest, holy and frequented by twice-born sages.

sanskrit: pitāmahasaraḥ puṇyaṃ puṣkaraṃ nāma bhārata vaikhānasānāṃ siddhānām ṛṣīṇām āśramaḥ priyaḥ
english: O Bharata, there is the sacred lake of the Grandsire called Pushkara, the beloved hermitage of the perfected Vaikhanasa sages.

sanskrit: apy atra saṃstavārthāya prajāpatir atho jagau puṣkareṣu kuruśreṣṭha gāthāṃ sukṛtināṃ vara
english: Even here, O best of the Kurus, Prajapati sang a praise-song for Pushkara — a verse glorifying the meritorious, O best among the virtuous.

sanskrit: manasāpy abhikāmasya puṣkarāṇi manasvinaḥ pāpāṇi vipraṇaśyanti nākapṛṣṭhe ca modate
english: For the wise person who desires Pushkara even in mind alone, sins are destroyed and he rejoices on the ridge of heaven.

sanskrit: dhaumya uvāca udīcyāṃ rājaśārdūla diśi puṇyāni yāni vai tāni te kīrtayiṣyāmi puṇyāny āyatanāni ca
english: Dhaumya said: O tiger among kings, I shall now describe to you the sacred things and holy shrines that exist in the northern direction.

sanskrit: sarasvatī puṇyavahā hradinī vanamālinī samudragā mahāvegā yamunā yatra pāṇḍava
english: O Pandava, there the Sarasvati flows with sacred waters, full of lakes, garlanded with forests, and the Yamuna flows toward the ocean with great speed.

sanskrit: tatra puṇyatamaṃ tīrthaṃ plakṣāvataraṇaṃ śivam yatra sārasvatair iṣṭvā gacchanty avabhṛthaṃ dvijāḥ
english: There is the most sacred, auspicious ford called Plakshavarana, where twice-born sages who have worshipped at Sarasvata tirthas go for the final purificatory bath.

sanskrit: puṇyaṃ cākhyāyate divyaṃ śivam agniśiro 'nagha sahadevo 'yajad yatra śamyākṣepeṇa bhārata
english: O sinless one, O Bharata, the divine and auspicious Agni-shiras is also described as sacred — there Sahadeva worshipped by the throwing of the shami stick.

sanskrit: etasminn eva cārtheyam indragītā yudhiṣṭhira gāthā carati loke 'smin gīyamānā dvijātibhiḥ
english: Regarding this very place, O Yudhishthira, there circulates in this world a verse sung by Indra, being sung by the twice-born.

sanskrit: agnayaḥ sahadevena ye citā yamunām anu śataṃ śatasahasrāṇi sahasraśatadakṣiṇāḥ
english: The fires kindled by Sahadeva along the Yamuna numbered a hundred times a hundred thousand, each with a thousand hundredfold sacrificial gifts.

sanskrit: tatraiva bharato rājā cakravartī mahāyaśāḥ viṃśatiṃ sapta cāṣṭau ca hayamedhān upāharat
english: There too, King Bharata, the great wheel-turning emperor of great fame, performed twenty-seven and eight horse sacrifices.

sanskrit: kāmakṛd yo dvijātīnāṃ śrutas tāta mayā purā atyantam āśramaḥ puṇyaḥ sarakas tasya viśrutaḥ
english: O dear one, I have heard of one who was a wish-fulfiller for the twice-born; his utterly holy and renowned hermitage called Saraka is famous.

sanskrit: sarasvatī nadī sadbhiḥ satataṃ pārtha pūjitā vālakhilyair mahārāja yatreṣṭam ṛṣibhiḥ purā
english: O Partha, the river Sarasvati is ever honoured by the virtuous; O great king, there the Valakhilya sages formerly performed their desired sacrifices.

sanskrit: dṛṣadvatī puṇyatamā tatra khyātā yudhiṣṭhira tatra vaivarṇyavarṇau ca supuṇyau manujādhipa
english: O Yudhishthira, the most sacred Drishadwati is renowned there; and there, O lord of men, two figures of differing colour are most holy.

sanskrit: vedajñau vedaviditau vidyāvedavidāv ubhau yajantau kratubhir nityaṃ puṇyair bharatasattama
english: Both are knowers of the Vedas, known through the Vedas, masters of knowledge and Veda — both ever worshipping with sacred rites, O best of Bharatas.

sanskrit: sametya bahuśo devāḥ sendrāḥ savaruṇāḥ purā viśākhayūpe 'tapyanta tasmāt puṇyatamaḥ sa vai
english: Long ago the gods together with Indra and Varuna repeatedly gathered and performed austerities at the Vishakha sacrificial post — therefore that place is the most sacred.

sanskrit: ṛṣir mahān mahābhāgo jamadagnir mahāyaśāḥ palāśakeṣu puṇyeṣu ramyeṣv ayajatābhibhūḥ
english: The great, greatly fortunate sage Jamadagni of great fame, who overcomes all, worshipped in the sacred and lovely Palashaka forests.

sanskrit: yatra sarvāḥ saricchreṣṭhāḥ sākṣāt tam ṛṣisattamam svaṃ svaṃ toyam upādāya parivāryopatasthire
english: There all the foremost rivers, bringing their own waters, surrounded and attended upon that best of sages in person.

sanskrit: api cātra mahārāja svayaṃ viśvāvasur jagau imaṃ ślokaṃ tadā vīra prekṣya vīryaṃ mahātmanaḥ
english: Moreover, O great king, O hero, Vishvavasu himself sang this verse there upon witnessing the might of that great-souled one.

sanskrit: yajamānasya vai devāñ jamadagner mahātmanaḥ āgamya saritaḥ sarvā madhunā samatarpayan
english: When the great-souled Jamadagni was performing the sacrifice, all the rivers came there and satisfied the gods with sweet water.

sanskrit: gandharvayakṣarakṣobhir apsarobhiś ca śobhitam kirātakiṃnarāvāsaṃ śailaṃ śikhariṇāṃ varam
english: That best of peaked mountains, adorned with gandharvas, yakshas, rakshasas and apsaras, is the dwelling of kiratas and kinnaras.

sanskrit: bibheda tarasā gaṅgā gaṅgādvāre yudhiṣṭhira puṇyaṃ tat khyāyate rājan brahmarṣigaṇasevitam
english: O Yudhishthira, there the Ganga burst through with great force at Gangadvara; O king, that sacred place is renowned, frequented by hosts of brahmin sages.

sanskrit: sanatkumāraḥ kauravya puṇyaṃ kanakhalaṃ tathā parvataś ca purur nāma yatra jātaḥ purūravāḥ
english: O descendant of Kuru, Sanatkumara is associated with the sacred Kankahala; and there is the mountain named Puru, where Pururavas was born.

sanskrit: bhṛgur yatra tapas tepe maharṣigaṇasevitaḥ sa rājann āśramaḥ khyāto bhṛgutuṅgo mahāgiriḥ
english: O king, the hermitage where Bhrigu performed austerities attended by hosts of great sages is renowned — the great mountain called Bhrigu-tunga.

sanskrit: yac ca bhūtaṃ bhaviṣyac ca bhavac ca puruṣarṣabha nārāyaṇaḥ prabhur viṣṇuḥ śāśvataḥ puruṣottamaḥ
english: O bull among men, whatever has existed, will exist, and exists now — Narayana is the lord, Vishnu the eternal, the highest of beings.

sanskrit: tasyātiyaśasaḥ puṇyāṃ viśālāṃ badarīm anu āśramaḥ khyāyate puṇyas triṣu lokeṏu viśrutaḥ
english: Along the sacred and vast Badari of that supremely glorious one, there is known a sacred hermitage, renowned in all three worlds.

sanskrit: uṣṇatoyavahā gaṅga śītatoyavahāparā suvarṇasikatā rājan viśālāṃ badarīm anu
english: O king, along the vast Badari, one tributary of the Ganga carries warm water and another carries cold water; one has golden sands.

sanskrit: ṛṣayo yatra devāś ca mahābhāgā mahaujasaḥ prāpya nityaṃ namasyanti devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ vibhum
english: There, sages and gods of great fortune and great power, having reached that place, constantly bow in reverence to the divine and all-pervading Narayana.

sanskrit: yatra nārāyaṇo devaḥ paramātmā sanātanaḥ tatra kṛtsnaṃ jagat pārtha tīrthāny āyatanāni ca
english: O Partha, wherever the divine Narayana, the eternal Supreme Self, abides — there is the entire universe, all the sacred fords and holy shrines.

sanskrit: tat puṇyaṃ tat paraṃ brahma tat tīrthaṃ tat tapovanam tatra devarṣayaḥ siddhāḥ sarve caiva tapodhanāḥ
english: That is the sacred, that is the supreme Brahman, that is the ford, that is the forest of austerity; there all divine sages and perfected ones and those whose wealth is austerity dwell.

sanskrit: ādidevo mahāyogī yatrāste madhusūdanaḥ puṇyānām api tat puṇyaṃ tatra te saṃśayo 'stu mā
english: Where the primeval god, the great yogi Madhusudana dwells — that is the most sacred even among sacred things; let there be no doubt in you about that.

sanskrit: etāni rājan puṇyāni pṛthivyāṃ pṛthivīpate kīrtitāni naraśreṣṭha tīrthāny āyatanāni ca
english: O king, O lord of the earth, O best of men, these sacred fords and holy shrines upon the earth have now been described.

sanskrit: etāni vasubhiḥ sādhyair ādityair marudaśvibhiḥ ṛṣibhir brahmakalpaiś ca sevitāni mahātmabhiḥ
english: These have been frequented by the Vasus, the Sadhyas, the Adityas, the Maruts, the Ashvins, and by great-souled sages who are equal to Brahma.

sanskrit: caran etāni kaunteya sahito brāhmaṇarṣabhaiḥ bhrātṛbhiś ca mahābhāgair utkaṇṭhāṃ vijahiṣyasi
english: O Kaunteya, wandering to these places together with the foremost brahmins and your greatly blessed brothers, you will cast off your longing and grief.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evaṃ saṃbhāṣamāṇe tu dhaumye kauravanandana lomaśaḥ sumahātejā ṛṣis tatrājagāma ha
english: Vaishampayana said: O joy of the Kurus, while Dhaumya was thus conversing, the sage Lomasha of very great splendor arrived there.

sanskrit: taṃ pāṇḍavāgrajo rājā sagaṇo brāhmaṇāś ca te udatiṣṭhan mahābhāgaṃ divi śakram ivāmarāḥ
english: The eldest of the Pandavas, the king, along with his companions and those brahmins, stood up for that greatly blessed one, as the immortals stand for Shakra in heaven.

sanskrit: tam abhyarcya yathānyāyaṃ dharmarājo yudhiṣṭhiraḥ papracchāgamane hetum aṭane ca prayojanam
english: The Dharma-king Yudhishthira, having duly honoured him, asked the reason for his coming and the purpose of his wandering.

sanskrit: sa pṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍuputreṇa prīyamāṇo mahāmanāḥ uvāca ślakṣṇayā vācā harṣayann iva pāṇḍavān
english: Asked by the son of Pandu, the great-minded one, filled with affection, spoke in a gentle voice, as if gladdening the Pandavas.

sanskrit: saṃcarann asmi kaunteya sarvalokān yadṛcchayā gataḥ śakrasya sadanaṃ tatrāpaśyaṃ sureśvaram
english: I was wandering through all the worlds at will, O Kaunteya; having gone to the abode of Shakra, I saw the lord of the gods there.

sanskrit: tava ca bhrātaraṃ vīram apaśyaṃ savyasācinam śakrasyārdhāsanagataṃ tatra me vismayo mahān āsīt puruṣaśārdūla dṛṣṭvā pārthaṃ tathāgatam
english: And I saw your heroic brother, the ambidextrous Arjuna, seated on half of Shakra's throne; seeing Partha thus arrived there, O tiger among men, great was my wonder.

sanskrit: āha māṃ tatra deveśo gaccha pāṇḍusutān iti so 'ham abhyāgataḥ kṣipraṃ didṛkṣus tvāṃ sahānujam
english: The lord of gods spoke to me there: 'Go to the sons of Pandu.' So I have come quickly, wishing to see you together with your brothers.

sanskrit: vacanāt puruhūtasya pārthasya ca mahātmanaḥ ākhyāsye te priyaṃ tāta mahat pāṇḍavanandana
english: By the command of Puruhuta and the great-souled Partha, O dear Pandava-joy, I shall tell you something greatly pleasing.

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiḥ sahito rājan kṛṣṇayā caiva tac chṛṇu yat tvayokto mahābāhur astrārthaṃ pāṇḍavarṣabha
english: O king, hear this together with your brothers and Krishna — that which the mighty-armed Arjuna, bull among Pandavas, was asked by you for the sake of weapons.

sanskrit: tad astram āptaṃ pārthena rudrād apratimaṃ mahat yat tad brahmaśiro nāma tapasā rudram āgatam
english: That weapon has been obtained by Partha from Rudra — the incomparable and great weapon called Brahma-shiras, which came to Rudra through austerity.

sanskrit: amṛtād utthitaṃ raudraṃ tal labdhaṃ savyasācinā tat samantraṃ sasaṃhāraṃ saprāyaścittamaṅgalam
english: That fearsome weapon born from amrita has been obtained by the ambidextrous Arjuna — along with its mantras, its withdrawal formula, its expiation rite and auspicious ceremony.

sanskrit: vajraṃ cānyāni cāstrāṇi daṇḍādīni yudhiṣṭhira yamāt kuberād varuṇād indrāc ca kurunandana astrāṇy adhītavān pārtho divyāny amitavikramaḥ
english: O Yudhishthira, O joy of the Kurus, Partha of boundless valour has also learned the thunderbolt and other weapons — the rod and others — from Yama, Kubera, Varuna, and Indra, all divine weapons.

sanskrit: viśvāvasoś ca tanayād gītaṃ nṛttaṃ ca sāma ca vāditraṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ pratyavindad yathāvidhi
english: And from the son of Vishvavasu he has properly and duly acquired singing, dancing, chanting of samans, and instrumental music.

sanskrit: evaṃ kṛtāstraḥ kaunteyo gāndharvaṃ vedam āptavān sukhaṃ vasati bībhatsur anujasyānujas tava
english: Thus Kaunteya Bibhatsu, having mastered weapons and acquired the Gandharva-veda, dwells happily — he who is the younger brother of your younger brother.

sanskrit: yadarthaṃ māṃ suraśreṣṭha idaṃ vacanam abravīt tac ca te kathayiṣyāmi yudhiṣṭhira nibodha me
english: The purpose for which the best of gods spoke this message to me — that too I shall tell you, O Yudhishthira; hear me attentively.

sanskrit: bhavān manuṣyalokāya gamiṣyati na saṃśayaḥ brūyād yudhiṣṭhiraṃ tatra vacanān me dvijottama
english: 'You will certainly go to the world of men; there, O best of twice-born, speak to Yudhishthira on my behalf' — thus said he.

sanskrit: āgamiṣyati te bhrātā kṛtāstraḥ kṣipram arjunaḥ surakāryaṃ mahat kṛtvā yad āśakyaṃ divaukasaiḥ
english: Your brother Arjuna, having mastered weapons, will come to you soon, having accomplished a great task for the gods — one which even the celestials could not achieve.

sanskrit: tapasā tu tvam ātmānaṃ bhrātṛbhiḥ saha yojaya tapaso hi paraṃ nāsti tapasā vindate mahat
english: But you — engage yourself along with your brothers in austerity; for there is nothing higher than austerity, and through austerity one obtains great things.

sanskrit: ahaṃ ca karṇaṃ jānāmi yathāvad bharatarṣabha na sa pārthasya saṃgrāme kalām arhati ṣoḍaśīm
english: And I know Karna truly, O bull of the Bharatas — in battle against Partha, he is not worth a sixteenth part.

sanskrit: yac cāpi te bhayaṃ tasmān manasistham ariṃdama tac cāpy apahariṣyāmi savyasācāv ihāgate
english: And whatever fear of him lies in your heart, O subduer of foes — that too I shall remove when the ambidextrous Arjuna arrives here.

sanskrit: yac ca te mānasaṃ vīra tīrthayātrām imāṃ prati tac ca te lomaśaḥ sarvaṃ kathayiṣyaty asaṃśayam
english: And whatever is in your mind, O hero, regarding this pilgrimage to the sacred fords — all of that Lomasha will certainly tell you without doubt.

sanskrit: yac ca kiṃ cit tapoyuktaṃ phalaṃ tīrtheṣu bhārata maharṣir eṣa yad brūyāt tac chraddheyam ananyathā
english: And whatever fruit connected with austerity is found at the sacred fords, O Bharata — whatever this great sage says, that is to be trusted without any doubt.

sanskrit: lomaśa uvāca dhanaṃjayena cāpy uktaṃ yat tac chṛṇu yudhiṣṭhira yudhiṣṭhiraṃ bhrātaraṃ me yojayer dharmyayā śriyā
english: Lomasha said: O Yudhishthira, hear also what was said by Dhananjaya: 'You should unite my brother Yudhishthira with righteous prosperity.'

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi dharmān parān vettha tapāṃsi ca tapodhana śrīmatāṃ cāpi jānāsi rājñāṃ dharmaṃ sanātanam
english: For you know the highest dharmas and austerities, O wealth of austerity, and you know the eternal dharma of prosperous kings.

sanskrit: sa bhavān yat paraṃ veda pāvanaṃ puruṣān prati tena saṃyojayethās tvaṃ tīrthapuṇyena pāṇḍavam
english: Let you, who know what is highest and purifying for men, unite this Pandava with the merit of the sacred fords.

sanskrit: yathā tīrthāni gaccheta gāś ca dadyāt sa pārthivaḥ tathā sarvātmanā kāryam iti māṃ vijayo 'bravīt
english: 'That king should visit the sacred fords and donate cows — this should be done with one's whole soul' — thus Vijaya spoke to me.

sanskrit: bhavatā cānugupto 'sau caret tīrthāni sarvaśaḥ rakṣobhyo rakṣitavyaś ca durgeṣu viṣameṣu ca
english: Protected by you, he should wander to all the sacred fords; and he must be guarded from rakshasas in difficult and dangerous places.

sanskrit: dadhīca iva devendraṃ yathā cāpy aṅgirā ravim tathā rakṣasva kaunteyaṃ rākṣasebhyo dvijottama
english: As Dadhicha protected the lord of the gods, and as Angiras protected the sun, so protect this son of Kunti from the rakshasas, O best of twice-born.

sanskrit: yātudhānā hi bahavo rākṣasāḥ parvatopamāḥ tvayābhiguptān kaunteyān nātivarteyur antikāt
english: For many flesh-eating rakshasas, mountain-like in size, would not be able to approach the sons of Kunti when they are under your protection.

sanskrit: so 'ham indrasya vacanān niyogād arjunasya ca rakṣamāṇo bhayebhyas tvāṃ cariṣyāmi tvayā saha
english: Therefore I, by the command of Indra and the commission of Arjuna, protecting you from dangers, will wander together with you.

sanskrit: dvis tīrthāni mayā pūrvaṃ dṛṣṭāni kurunandana idaṃ tṛtīyaṃ drakṣyāmi tāny eva bhavatā saha
english: O joy of the Kurus, I have previously visited the sacred fords twice; this will be my third visit, and I shall see those same fords together with you.

sanskrit: iyaṃ rājarṣibhir yātā puṇyakṛdbhir yudhiṣṭhira manvādibhir mahārāja tīrthayātrā bhayāpahā
english: O Yudhishthira, O great king, this pilgrimage to sacred fords, which was undertaken by royal sages beginning with Manu who had accumulated merit, dispels fear.
